H6030: properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extension to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce
H347: Ijob, the patriarch famous for his patience
H4100: properly, interrogative what? (including how? why? when?); but also exclamation, what! (including how!), or indefinitely what (including whatever, and even relatively, that which); often used with prefixes in various adverbial or conjunctive senses
H5826: to surround, i.e. protect or aid
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H3581: vigor, literally (force, in a good or a bad sense) or figuratively (capacity, means, produce); also (from its hardiness) a large lizard
H3467: properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor
H2220: the arm (as stretched out), or (of animals) the foreleg; figuratively, force
H5797: strength in various applications (force, security, majesty, praise)
H3289: to advise; reflexively, to deliberate or resolve
H8454: support or (by implication) ability, i.e. (direct) help, (in purpose) an undertaking, (intellectual) understanding
H3045: to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
H854: properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc.
H4310: who? (occasionally, by a peculiar idiom, of things); also (indefinitely) whoever; often used in oblique construction with prefix or suffix
H5046: properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise
H4405: a word; collectively, a discourse; figuratively, a topic
H5397: a puff, i.e. wind, angry or vital breath, divine inspiration, intellect. or (concretely) an animal
H3318: to go (causatively, bring) out, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, direct and proxim.
H4480: properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of in many senses
H7496: properly, lax, i.e. (figuratively) a ghost (as dead; in plural only)
H2342: properly, to twist or whirl (in a circular or spiral manner), i.e. (specifically) to dance, to writhe in pain (especially of parturition) or fear; figuratively, to wait, to pervert
H8478: the bottom (as depressed); only adverbially, below (often with prepositional prefix underneath), in lieu of, etc.
H4325: water; figuratively, juice; by euphemism, urine, semen
H7931: to reside or permanently stay (literally or figuratively)
H7585: Hades or the world of the dead (as if a subterranean retreat), including its accessories and inmates
H5048: a front, i.e. part opposite; specifically a counterpart, or mate; usually (adverbial, especially with preposition) over against or before
H369: a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle
H5186: to stretch or spread out; by implication, to bend away (including moral deflection); used in a great variety of application
H6828: properly, hidden, i.e. dark; used only of the north as aquarter (gloomy and unknown)
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H8414: a desolation (of surface), i.e. desert; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain
H776: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
H6887: to cramp, literally or figuratively, transitive or intransitive
H5645: properly, an envelope, i.e. darkness (or density, 2 Chronicles 4:17); specifically, a (scud) cloud; also a copse
H1234: to cleave; generally, to rend, break, rip or open
H6051: a cloud (as covering the sky), i.e. the nimbus or thunder-cloud
H270: to seize (often with the accessory idea of holding in possession)
H6440: the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.)
H3678: properly, covered, i.e. a throne (as canopied)
H2706: an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage)
H5704: as far (or long, or much) as, whether of space (even unto) or time (during, while, until) or degree (equally with)
H216: illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.)
H5973: adverb or preposition, with (i.e. in conjunction with), in varied applications; specifically, equally with; often with prepositional prefix (and then usually unrepresented in English)
H2822: the dark; hence (literally) darkness; figuratively, misery, destruction, death, ignorance, sorrow, wickedness
H5982: a column (as standing); also a stand, i.e. platform
H8064: the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)
H7322: properly, to triturate (in a mortar), i.e. (figuratively) to agitate (by concussion)
H7280: properly, to toss violently and suddenly (the sea with waves, the skin with boils); figuratively (in a favorable manner) to settle, i.e. quiet; specifically, to wink (from the motion of the eye-lids)
H3220: a sea (as breaking in noisy surf) or large body of water; specifically (with the article), the Mediterranean Sea; sometimes a large river, or an artifical basin; locally, the west, or (rarely) the south
H8394: intelligence; by implication, an argument; by extension, caprice
H4272: to dash asunder; by implication, to crush, smash or violently plunge; figuratively, to subdue or destroy
H7307: wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension, a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit, but only of a rational being (including its expression and functions)
H2490: properly, to bore, i.e. (by implication) to wound, to dissolve; figuratively, to profane (a person, place or thing), to break (one's word), to begin (as if by an 'opening wedge'); to play (the flute)
H3027: a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.),
H1281: a fugitive, i.e. the serpent (as fleeing), and the constellation by that name
H1870: a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb
H1697: a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause
H8085: to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
H1369: force (literally or figuratively); by implication, valor, victory
H995: to separate mentally (or distinguish), i.e.(generally) understand
